title: Protocol to measure calcium spikes in cardiomyocytes obtained from human pluripotent stem cells using a ready-to-use media
protocol: Warm at least 1 mL of Accutase and 6 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell at 37°C for 3–5 min.
Remove the old medium from hESCs.
Wash cells with 2 mL of DPBS.
Add 1 mL of Accutase to the well containing hESCs.
Incubate in a humidified incubator at 37°C for 3 min.
Observe cells under an inverted microscope to confirm cell detachment.
Incubate at 37°C for an additional minute if cells have not evenly detached.
Add 1 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell and gently pipette up and down 2–3 times to obtain a single cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 110 g for 3 min at 21°C–24°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet with 6 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell. Avoid excessive pipetting to reduce cell stress.
Dispense 1 mL of cell resuspension into each well of the vitronectin pre-coated 6-well plate.
Move the plate using a stretched-eight-like motion, followed by a cross-like motion to distribute cells homogeneously in each well.
Place the plate on a 37°C hot plate or flat surface for 5 min to allow cell attachment.
Keep hESCs in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 21% O2.
Warm complete E8 medium at 37°C for 3–5 min.
Remove the old medium and add 2 mL of complete E8 medium per well.
Replace the medium daily and passage cells once the confluency reaches 70%.
Warm at least 1 mL of Versene and 6 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell at 37°C for 3–5 minutes.
Remove the old medium and wash with 2 mL of DPBS.
Add 1 mL of Versene and incubate at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Observe the cells under an inverted microscope to confirm that cells remain attached but slightly separated and colonies have curled edges.
Incubate at 37°C for an additional minute if cells do not show these features, otherwise proceed to the next step.
Remove the Versene with caution to avoid cell detachment.
Add 2 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell.
Gently detach the cells from the plate by pipetting 1–2 times using a P1000 pipette and transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Avoid excessive pipetting to reduce cell stress.
Add 4 mL of complete E8 medium supplemented with RevitaCell to the cell suspension (6 mL total volume).
Mix gently by inverting the tube.
Dispense 1 mL of cell resuspension into each well of a Matrigel pre-coated 6-well plate.
Move the plate using a stretched-eight-like motion followed by a cross-like motion to distribute cells homogeneously in each well.
Place the plate on a 37°C hot plate or flat surface for 5 minutes to allow cell attachment.
Keep hiPSCs in a humidified incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 and 5% O2.
Achieve 70% confluence of hPSCs.
Passage hPSCs at ratios of 1:8, 1:10, and 1:12.
Remove old medium containing RevitaCell.
Add 2 mL of complete E8 medium per well.
Ensure cell confluency is around the desired level for differentiation induction.
Carefully remove E8 medium from the hPSCs.
Add 2 mL of warm Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Medium A per well.
Aspirate and add differentiation media slowly at every media change.
Set the incubator temperature at 33°C degrees on day 0 to improve differentiation efficiency and homogeneity of contracting cells in the dish.
Carefully remove medium A and add 2 mL of warm Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Medium B per well.
Remove the medium B from the wells.
Add 2 mL of warm Cardiomyocyte Maintenance Medium per well.
Check that the cell monolayer reaches 100% confluency.
Change the Cardiomyocyte Maintenance Medium every other day from days 6 to 40.
Monitor for spontaneous beating or heterogeneous contraction starting at days 12 to 18.
Check troubleshooting section, problem 2 and 3 if no detectable spontaneous beating or homogeneous contraction after 18 days.
Perform downstream assays before day 24 to minimize cell detachment risk.
Seed hPSCs on pre-coated coverslips in a 24-well plate at ratios of 1:6, 1:8, or 1:10 for immunofluorescence characterization.
Test expression of transcription factor NKX2.5 as early cardiac mesoderm marker.
Test expression of TNNT2/cTNT as cardiomyocyte marker involved in muscle contraction.
Thaw Immunocytochemistry kit reagents and store them at 4°C for up to six months.
Warm the 10× wash buffer at 21°C–24°C and mix well before use.
Prepare 2,100 μL of 1× wash buffer per each well by diluting 210 μL of 10× wash buffer in 1,890 μL of MilliQ water.
Remove the old media from the cells and wash each well with 500 μL of DPBS.
Move the 24-well plate containing the coverslips inside a fume hood carefully.
Add 300 μL of fixative solution (4% formaldehyde in DPBS) per well and incubate for 15 min at 21°C–24°C.
Remove the fixative solution and add 300 μL of 1× wash buffer per well.
Cover the wells containing the coverslips with parafilm to prevent drying and store at 4°C for up to a month.
Remove the wash buffer from the wells.
Add 300 μL of permeabilization solution (1% Saponin in DPBS) to each well.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 21°C–24°C.
Remove the permeabilization solution from the wells.
Add 300 μL of blocking solution to each well.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 21°C–24°C.
Prepare a humidified chamber by placing a blotting paper soaked in water in a squared plastic dish.
Place a piece of parafilm on top of the soaked paper, ensuring it fits the number of coverslips to process.
Use a towel paper to flatten the parafilm on top of the soaked blotting paper, removing all wrinkles and bubbles.
Prepare 40 μL of 25× working dilution of each primary antibody (rabbit α-NKX2.5 & mouse α-TNNT2) by diluting 1 μL of antibody stock 1000× in 39 μL of blocking solution.
Store the diluted antibodies at 4°C adequately labeled.
Prepare 25 μL of diluted antibodies (1×) per each coverslip by diluting 1 μL of 25× working dilution of each antibody in 23 μL of blocking buffer.
Dispense a 25 μL drop of the 1× diluted mix containing both antibodies on the parafilm per each coverslip to be stained.
Handle the coverslip with forceps, ensuring the cell side faces up.
Remove excess buffer from the coverslip by gently touching the rim with torn blot paper.
Place the coverslip on top of the antibody drop with the cell side facing down.
Incubate at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Add 300 μL of 1× wash buffer in each well of a 24-well plate and keep it aside.
Add 100 μL of DPBS at the rim of each coverslip to lift the coverslip from the parafilm.
Take the coverslip from the parafilm and place it in a well.
Incubate for 3 min at 21°C–24°C.
Remove the wash buffer and perform two additional washes with 300 μL of 1× wash buffer.

Prepare 10 μL of 25× working dilution of each secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 488 Donkey α-mouse & Alexa Fluor 594 Donkey α-rabbit) by diluting 1 μL of antibody stock 250× in 9 μL of blocking solution.
Store diluted antibodies at 4°C adequately labeled, protected from light.
Prepare 25 μL of diluted antibodies (1×) per each coverslip by diluting 1 μL of 25× working dilution of each antibody in 23 μL of blocking buffer.
Dispense a 25 μL drop of the 1× diluted mix containing both antibodies on the parafilm per each sample to stain.
Incubate for 1 h at 21°C–24°C.
Proceed with washing step as described previously with the primary antibody step (16).
Add a drop of ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mounting solution with DAPI on
Use a wipe to remove air bubbles and keep the vial upside down.
Add a drop of mounting solution per sample onto a clean slide.
Mount up to 3 samples per slide.
Take the coverslip from the well and remove residual buffer drops with a gentle touch of torn blot paper on the coverslip rim.
Place the coverslip on top of the mounting media drop with the cell side facing down.
Incubate mounted coverslips at 21°C–24°C for 12–16 hours in the dark.
Seal the coverslip edges with epoxy glue.
Proceed to acquisition or store the samples at -20°C for long-term storage.
Warm 1 mL of trypsin-EDTA 0.25% at 37°C for 3–5 min.
Discard the old media and wash with 2 mL of DBPS.
Add 1 mL of trypsin-EDTA 0.25% and incubate in a humidified incubator at 37°C for 5–15 min.
Check the cells using an inverted microscope every 5 min.
Proceed to the next step when the cells are detaching from the plate and become round.
Add 3 mL of DPBS and pipette up and down 2-3 times using a P1000 pipette to obtain a single cell suspension, avoiding excessive pipetting to reduce cell stress and viability.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and mix gently with 10 μL of trypan blue.
Mix 1.5 ml eppendorf tubes with 1 x 10^6 cells for each cell line.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of BD cytofix fixation buffer.
Incubate for 20 min at 21°C–24°C with gentle agitation in a rocker.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Wash twice with 500 μL of DPBS.
Mix 350 μl of 10× BD perm/wash solution with 3150 μl of MilliQ water.
Wash twice with 100 μl of 1× BD perm/wash solution.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 100 μl of 1× BD perm/wash solution and incubate for 10 min at 21°C–24°C with gentle agitation in a rocker.
Incubate samples at 21°C–24°C for 45 minutes with gentle agitation in a rocker.
Centrifuge the mixture at 500 g for 3 minutes and discard the supernatant.
Wash twice with 500 μL of 1× BD perm/wash solution.
Dissolve 0.1 g of BSA in 20 mL of DPBS by vortexing for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 400 μL of BSA 0.5% and transfer the cell suspension into a 5 mL round bottom tube passing through a 35-μm mesh strainer.
Acquire data using a flow cytometer equipped with a blue laser (488 nm) and a filter 530/30 nm to record FITC emission.
Fill the water reservoir of the stage incubator up to the maximum level.
Turn on the microscope 30 minutes before use.
Set the temperature to 37°C in the stage incubator.
Set the humidity to 80% in the stage incubator.
Insert a template plate on the plate holder while the instrument calibrates.
Launch the EVOS FL Auto 2 software and set correct incubator parameters in the control panel tab.
Select an objective lens with 0.3 NA/10× magnification and long working distance suitable for plastic bottom dishes (WD = 9.2 mm).
Choose the “Live recording” option corresponding to a camera setting of about 20 fps.
To acquire at ≤ 10 fps, use the "as fast as possible" option from the ‘Time Lapse’ tab in the EVOS FL software.
Alternatively, set parameters for the desired frame rate using the EVOS FL software.
Prepare the Fluo-4 AM NW loading solution as described in the materials and equipment section.
Carefully remove culturing media from beating cardiomyocytes using a P1000 pipette to avoid cell detachment and wash once with DPBS.
Aspirate the DPBS with a P1000 pipette and load 1 ml of Fluo-4 AM NW solution into the well.
Place the cells in an incubator set at 37°C for 45 min.
Remove Fluo-4 AM NW solution from hPSC-CMs.
Add 1.5 mL of CMs Maintenance Medium.
Incubate hPSC-CMs for 10 min inside the stage chamber for equilibration.

Use inverted EVOS FL Auto2 microscope equipped with a 10× objective and a pixel size of 0.88 μm to select the first Region of Interest (ROI) in brightfield mode using low illumination intensity (0.50 msec).
Draw a straight line of approximately 200 μm using the “line tool” in a random area of the field.
In the ROI Manager window, click “Add” to save the selected region for analysis.
Draw and record the coordinates of multiple lines in the ROI Manager window.
Select the line from the ROI Manager menu.
Use the ImageJ function “Image > Stacks > Reslice” to generate the kymograph.
Check the options: Rotate 90 degrees and avoid interpolation to visualize the frames over time in the horizontal axes and the distance in the vertical axes.
Acquire sequential images labelled from one to five for each condition.
Excite the Fluo-4 AM loaded cells with the GFP LED light cube at 494 nm and collect emission fluorescence signal at 516 nm.
Use the fine focus control of the microscope to bring the sample into the sharpest possible focus with a fine adjustment knob.
Identify the plane where the cell edges appear sharp and not blurry.
Start the live imaging with the 10× objective by clicking “record”.
Launch ImageJ software and open the sequence of TIFF images you want to analyze using the command “File > Import > Image Sequence”.
Perform background correction on the imported image sequence in ImageJ.
Adjust the brightness and contrast of the movie to the desired level.
Draw a straight horizontal line of approximately 200 μm in a random area of the field.
Open the ROI Manager window with the command "Analyze > Tools > ROI manager".
In the ROI Manager window, click “Add” to save the coordinates of the straight-line selection.
Record the coordinates of multiple lines in the ROI Manager window for analysis of multiple ROIs.
Acquire five independent fields from a well of a 6-well plate.
Analyze five independent ROIs for each field.
Use the same ROI coordinates for all samples to reduce biased selection of beating areas.
Select the line from the ROI Manager menu.
Use the ImageJ function "ImageStacksReslice".
Check the options: "Rotate 90 degrees" and "avoid interpolation".
Visualize the frames over time in the horizontal axes and distance in the vertical axes.
Open a new window showing the spatial position over time of the selected areas.
Save the kymograph as a TIFF image with the command “FileSave as”.
Select the line from the ROI Manager menu again.
Measure the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of the area of interest over time.
